answer: In an agent marketplace trading opal, crystal, and umber pigment, each seller must lock a bond for 30 days, and its order quota is proportional to that bond. Quotas add linearly, so splitting the same funds across a thousand fake identities buys no more capacity than one identity. To flood the market, an attacker must lock proportionally more capital for the full period, sacrificing liquidity and the returns those funds could earn elsewhere.
